Quick note — we normally issue list-price invoices to the purchasing customer (BrightLayer) and record a separate reseller commission line in our internal ledger. For private offers where resellers need clear pass-through evidence, we have two operational patterns:

Pattern A (preferred for visibility):
- Invoice to BrightLayer shows full list price per SKU
- Separate credit line (or subsequent credit memo) for the reseller fee that reduces the net amount payable by BrightLayer
- We provide a reconciliation CSV that maps our SKU IDs -> reseller entity -> commission % and dollar amount

Pattern B (preferred for simpler AP workflows):
- Invoice to BrightLayer includes a distinct line item labeled "Reseller pass-through (MediServe)" with negative value applied, so the invoice net equals the amount after reseller pass-through
- Provides a clear single invoice for BrightLayer to pay and shows the reseller reduction on the face of the invoice

Both are feasible; Pattern B reduces accounting work on their side but requires us to show MediServe name on the invoice. Legal is usually okay with that for enterprise customers. If BrightLayer prefers not to show reseller name on the invoice, we should go Pattern A and provide a discrete reconciliation CSV they can ingest.

Connor — once you generate the sample, set up a short one-pager that explains which pattern we used and why. I’ll confirm the reseller fee % (we agreed to 8% in the deal sketch) and check with RevOps if any tax implications exist for the negative line.

Ben
Senior Channel Ops | Redwood Inference
